_comment: Measured values quoted by the deployment docs. Kept here rather than in prose
so a number appears in exactly one place and the reference is generated from it.
Every entry records how it was obtained, because a figure whose method is lost
cannot be re-checked and quietly becomes folklore.

tier.model_note: 390M = 512 MB less roughly 120 MB of OS. DO droplets ship swapless.

throughput_rps._method: 16 keep-alive connections, 8s per route, load driver outside the cap, all responses 2xx

memory._method: cgroup memory.peak after saturating every route
memory._ingest_note: Measured on the unit cgroup, not the MainPID. granian's supervisor forks a worker and the worker holds the memory; the earlier 34.7 MB figure was the supervisor and never moved under any load. The stack total was always a cgroup measurement and is unaffected.

build.note: memory.peak counts reclaimable page cache, so it is an upper bound on appetite, not a requirement

payload._method: every URL the service worker precaches, plus the three woff2 and the worker itself

ingest_amplification._method: largest body each cap accepts, filled with minimal valid events, measured against the written JSONL

service_worker._method: Chromium via Playwright, caches.keys() then an offline reload

test_counts._method: the suites in this repo and the scratch harnesses that produced these numbers

ingest_lifecycle._method: systemd socket activation with systemd-socket-proxyd --exit-idle-time, measured via MemoryCurrent
ingest_lifecycle.idle_state: inactive; the socket unit holds the port
ingest_lifecycle.note: MemoryHigh below the working set does not shrink the process, it wedges it in reclaim and startup never completes; 48M was tried and the service never became ready.
